mainEntity.name: How much does a Mercedes SLC 43 AMG engine replacement cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: A rebuilt M276 engine for the SLC 43 AMG costs £6,500-£9,600 supply-only. Fitting adds £1,200-£2,000 depending on complexity - AMG V6 biturbo work requires specialist knowledge.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of timing chain tensioner failure on a Mercedes SLC 43 AMG?

acceptedAnswer.text: A rattling or knocking noise on cold start lasting a few seconds is the classic warning sign on the M276 engine. The hydraulic secondary chain tensioners are a known weak point on the M276. If ignored, it can lead to chain stretch, poor timing performance, misfires and catastrophic engine failure.

mainEntity.name: What causes carbon buildup on a Mercedes SLC 43 AMG?

acceptedAnswer.text: Carbon buildup on intake valves is a known issue on direct injection engines like the M276. Because fuel is injected directly into the combustion chamber, intake valves are not washed by fuel, allowing carbon deposits to accumulate over time.

mainEntity.name: Is the Mercedes SLC 43 AMG engine (M276) reliable?

acceptedAnswer.text: The M276 is a hand-built AMG performance engine - powerful and refined, but it has known weaknesses. Timing chain tensioner wear, carbon buildup, turbocharger issues, and PCV system failures are the most common problems. Generally a durable, refined engine - 200,000+ km examples are common - but has well-documented weak points. With these addressed and regular maintenance, the engine is capable of 150,000+ miles.

mainEntity.name: How long do Mercedes SLC 43 AMG engines last?

acceptedAnswer.text: Properly maintained M276 engines routinely reach 150,000-200,000 miles before major work. Timing chain issues typically appear between 50,000-90,000 miles.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in my Mercedes SLC 43 AMG?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, if the SLC is otherwise in good condition with no rust or major transmission faults. A rebuilt M276 costs £6,500-£9,600 - far less than replacing a £18,000-£35,000 vehicle. SLC 43 AMG values remain strong for well-maintained examples, making engine replacement a worthwhile investment.

historyTimeline.h2: Mercedes Benz SLC 43 AMG - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The SLC 43 AMG launched in 2016 as the flagship performance variant of the R172 SLC range, replacing the V8-powered SLK 55 AMG with a downsized but potent 3.0-litre V6 biturbo. Powered by the M276.823 engine producing 367hp and 520Nm of torque, it delivered 0-100 km/h in 4.7 seconds - just one-tenth slower than its V8 predecessor while offering improved efficiency. Production continued until 2020 when the SLC was discontinued, making the SLC 43 AMG the final performance roadster from Mercedes in this lineage.

milestones.description: M276.823, 3.0L V6 biturbo, 390hp (SLC 43 AMG power upgrade)
2020 - Both power outputs paired with 9G-TRONIC sports transmission
End of SLC production; R172 platform retired

historyTimeline.closingNote: Every engine fitted to the Mercedes Benz SLC 43 AMG is covered below, with UK rebuilt pricing and known failure points - from M276 timing chain tensioner wear and carbon buildup to turbocharger and PCV system issues.

commonProblems.h2: Mercedes Benz SLC 43 AMG Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The SLC 43 AMG's M276 V6 biturbo is a hand-built AMG performance engine - powerful, responsive and the heart of Mercedes' compact roadster flagship. However, like any high-performance engine, it has well-documented weaknesses that can lead to significant repair costs. Timing chain tensioner wear, carbon buildup on intake valves, turbocharger issues, and PCV system failures are the most common problems driving replacement enquiries. Every rebuilt engine supplied through EnginesMarket includes upgraded components addressing these original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: M276 Timing Chain Tensioner Wear - The SLC 43 AMG's Most Critical Weakness
problems.rootCause: The M276 engine suffers from secondary chain tensioner issues, resulting in a rattling noise on cold starts. The hydraulic tensioners are extra-weak, made with a simple hard rubber bearing that can leak oil pressure. A failing timing chain tensioner typically produces a rattling or knocking sound from the front of the engine, especially when the engine is cold or during hard acceleration. If ignored, the timing chain can stretch, leading to poor timing performance and misfires.

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical 2016-2020 SLC 43 AMG is worth approximately £18,000-£35,000 depending on mileage and condition. These premium AMG roadsters retain strong values for well-maintained examples, making engine replacement a justifiable investment.
problems.recommendation: If your SLC 43 AMG exhibits a rattling noise on cold start, act immediately. The M276's secondary chain tensioners are a known critical weakness. Specialist timing chain tensioner replacement at £1,200-£1,800 is significantly cheaper than dealer rates. If the chain has jumped timing, a full rebuilt M276 engine with upgraded timing components is the only safe option. The M276 is a better engine than the M272, but you will have to replace timing chain components by no later than 250k miles on it.

problems.h4: M276 Carbon Buildup on Intake Valves - The Direct Injection Performance Drain
problems.rootCause: Direct injection engines like the M276 are prone to carbon accumulation on intake valves. Because fuel is injected directly into the combustion chamber, intake valves are not washed by fuel, allowing carbon deposits to build up over time. Symptoms include rough idle, reduced performance, and poor fuel economy.

problems.h4: M276 Turbocharger & PCV System Failures - The Twin-Turbo's Performance Challenges
problems.rootCause: The M276's twin-turbochargers can suffer from oil leaks, worn bearings, or clogged oil lines, causing loss of power, excessive smoke, and high-pitched noises. PCV system failures can cause oil leaks, excessive crankcase pressure, or smoking exhaust. Oil cooler leaks from deteriorated seals can cause visible oil leaks or mixing of oil and coolant.
